question: Can fixed binary questions derived from the ordinary permitted one-bit changes on the three local words reveal a CHSH excess on one supplied coherent preparation?
inputs: The old founder is fixed before settings at 001. Each of the two equal-input births has three permitted fresh words. Study B gives the joint distribution; the scorer must rebuild it from the words.
The two single-bit toggles swap permitted endpoints and fix refused endpoints. Use the signs of the adjacency of actual moves, equality of the fresh bits, and the common invariant of the toggles.
forbidden_inputs: An optimized read angle or distinct numeric labels for the fresh bits.
Treating the chosen spectral readings or coherent preparation as supplied by ordinary growth.
primary_observable: The 16 two-reader outcome probabilities under four setting pairs and their CHSH score, reconstructed both from the full nine-word state and on the two sibling classes.
control: Compare to names exchanged or complemented, to the diagonal mixture and coherent product with the same marginals, and to the reinforcement weighting preserving ordinary named-word marginals. Try both signs on the unused nullspace. Compare against a local choice which would remove the access to change.
resource_budget: Small fixed matrices of order at most nine and six local relabellings. Pilot a single correlation before a full run. Single CPU, 1 GiB cap; expected seconds.
first_executable_signal: Compute the first joint probability table from the two genuine toggles and the uniform common invariant.
stop_rule: Stop on the four fixed setting pairs after all probabilities, no-signalling, matched controls, sensitivity to loss of coherence and an independent calculation have been checked.
nonclaims: Derivation of coherence or the spectral measurement from ordinary value updates
Separation of two births on unrestricted founder states
Untargeted discovery, optimality among all settings, or a general probability law
